requirements.text: Inspect existing pipelines, templates, variables, and environments before proposing structure.
Keep branch, path, schedule, and resource triggers intentional.
Use least-privilege service connections scoped to the target and prefer workload identity federation over secrets.
requirements.source: internal-azure-devops SKILL.md Workflow step 4; Azure consolidation spec section 5

requirements.text: Keep secrets in secret variables, Key Vault-linked variable groups, or managed identity patterns, and never print them.
Use deployment jobs targeting environments with approvals or checks for production-like targets.
Pin task major versions and name agent images deliberately.
Make rollback and health checks explicit when deployment is in scope.
Run or name the focused YAML and pipeline validation available in the repository.
Route CLI execution to awesome-copilot-azure-devops-cli, general delivery strategy to internal-devops-core-principles, and Azure platform design to internal-azure.
Return the design, material risk, and next validation action, and add security controls and rollback only when material.
requirements.source: Azure consolidation spec section 5; decision D3

cases.prompt: Review and harden this Azure DevOps pipeline before we use it for production deploys.
cases.initial_state: The fixture pipeline hardcodes a password, prints it, uses an Owner connection across all subscriptions, triggers on every branch, and floats the agent image.
cases.expected_output: Findings for the hardcoded and printed secret, the over-privileged service connection, the wildcard trigger, and the unpinned image, with concrete fixes.

assertions.text: The response flags the hardcoded password and the echo that prints it.
The response flags the Owner connection across all subscriptions and proposes a scoped connection with workload identity federation.
The response flags the wildcard branch trigger.
The response flags the floating ubuntu-latest image or proposes a deliberate image choice.

forbidden_actions: Keep the secret in plain YAML.
Approve the pipeline for production unchanged.

cases.prompt: Add a production stage after staging in our Azure DevOps pipeline.
cases.initial_state: The pipeline has build and staging stages that use plain jobs.
cases.expected_output: A deployment job targeting a production environment with approvals or checks, a health check, and a rollback path.

assertions.text: The production stage uses a deployment job targeting an environment with approvals or checks.
The response includes a health check and a rollback path.

forbidden_actions: Deploy to production from a plain job without environment gates.

pass: Environment gate, health check, and rollback are explicit.
fail: The stage deploys ungated or has no rollback.

cases.prompt: Create a CI pipeline for the new service in this repository.
cases.initial_state: The repository already has shared templates under pipelines/templates and path-filtered triggers for other services.
cases.expected_output: The new pipeline reuses the existing templates and follows the path-filter convention.

assertions.text: The response inspects and reuses the existing templates instead of inventing a new structure.
The trigger is path-filtered to the new service.

forbidden_actions: Introduce a parallel template structure without reason.

fail: The pipeline ignores existing templates and triggers on every change.

cases.prompt: Run the nightly pipeline now with az pipelines run and show me the result.
cases.initial_state: The request asks for CLI execution, not pipeline design.
cases.expected_output: CLI execution is routed to awesome-copilot-azure-devops-cli.

assertions.text: The response routes CLI execution to awesome-copilot-azure-devops-cli.

forbidden_actions: Redesign the pipeline YAML for a CLI execution request.

pass: The CLI owner handles the command.
fail: The pipeline design workflow runs instead.

cases.prompt: I edited azure-pipelines.yml to add a test stage. Make sure it is valid.
cases.initial_state: The repository has a YAML linter configured in pre-commit.
cases.expected_output: The focused YAML validation is run or named, and remote pipeline validation is named as a gap if not available locally.

assertions.text: The response runs or names the repository YAML validation.
The response states which pipeline-level validation remains unverified.

forbidden_actions: Claim the pipeline is valid without any check.

pass: A concrete validation result or named gap is reported.

cases.prompt: Should our organization move from release branches to trunk-based delivery with feature flags?
cases.initial_state: The question is tool-neutral delivery strategy.
cases.expected_output: General delivery strategy is routed to internal-devops-core-principles; Azure DevOps specifics are offered only when requested.

assertions.text: The response routes the delivery-strategy decision to internal-devops-core-principles.

forbidden_actions: Answer a tool-neutral strategy question with pipeline YAML.

fail: The response produces Azure DevOps YAML.

queries.query: Review this azure-pipelines.yml for security issues.
Add a production environment with approvals to our Azure DevOps pipeline.
Move this Azure DevOps service connection to workload identity federation.
Split our Azure DevOps pipeline into reusable templates with parameters.
Link a Key Vault-backed variable group to the deploy stage.
Our ADO path triggers run on every docs change; fix them.
Add rollback and health checks to the Azure DevOps deployment job.
Pin tasks and the agent image in this Azure pipeline.
Run az pipelines run for the nightly build.
Choose trunk-based versus release-branch promotion in general.
Define RBAC for the Azure deployment subscription.
Fix this Terraform module applied by the pipeline.
Review this Dockerfile built by the pipeline.
Review the diff of this pipeline pull request.
